name: Schloss Mentlberg
kurzbeschreibung: Schloss Mentlberg on the southern slope of Innsbruck: a fairytale Late Historicist residence in the style of Loire châteaux, redesigned in 1890 by Heinrich von Bourbon.
beschreibung:
Overview

The romantic Schloss Mentlberg is perched on the sunny forested slope of the Mentlberg above the Innsbruck districts of Wilten and Sieglanger on the southwestern outskirts of the Tyrolean provincial capital. With its delicate round turrets, steep slate roofs, oriels, and battlements, this aristocratic estate resembles at first glance a French fairytale château of the Loire monarchs. Nestled in a landscaped park with mature trees, the heritage-listed castle grounds unite more than 700 years of architectural and noble history with picturesque panoramic views over the Inntal valley and the rugged limestone crags of the Nordkette.

History & Late Historicism

The documented beginnings of the manor date back to the early 14th century: in 1305, the estate was first recorded as Mennlinberg, named after its owner at the time, Heinrich Mennlin. For centuries, the residence remained in the possession of esteemed Tyrolean noble families, including the Counts of Spaur. However, the castle owes its distinctive architectural appearance today to French high nobility: in 1889, Prince Heinrich von Bourbon, Duke of Bardi (Count of Chambord), acquired the property as an imposing exile residence. Between 1890 and 1905, Duke Heinrich had the old manor fundamentally remodeled according to plans by renowned Viennese architects Joseph Schönherr and Josef Mayr in the style of Late Historicism and Neo-Renaissance. The famous French Renaissance châteaux of the Loire Valley, particularly the royal hunting estate Chambord, served as a direct architectural prototype. Notable architectural features include the delicate castle chapel of the Immaculate Conception with artistic stained-glass windows, the monumental staircase tower, and richly ornamented facade details. Following the duke's death, the State of Tyrol acquired the property in 1928. Since then, the castle has housed the Landwirtschaftliche Landeslehranstalt für Forstwirtschaft, which exemplarily pairs the preservation of this historical ensemble with specialized forestry training.

Visit & Getting There

The exterior of the castle and the surrounding paths through the estate can be viewed year-round from the outside free of charge. Because the interior is actively utilized as an educational center and state institute of Tyrol, the historical rooms are generally not open to the general public (exceptions include open cultural days, classical concerts, and forestry conferences). Arriving by public transport: From Innsbruck Hauptbahnhof, take city bus line T or C directly to the Sieglanger or Peter-Brüx-Weg stop; from there, a short, signposted uphill walk (approx. 7 minutes) leads to the castle gate at Mentlbergstraße 24. By car: Via the A12 motorway (exit Innsbruck West), continue along Egger-Lienz-Straße into the Sieglanger district and up towards Mentlberg (limited parking available along the street).

Tips

The castle grounds serve as an ideal starting point for relaxing walks through the mixed forest towards Lake Natterer See or along the sunny panoramic path towards the Bergiselschanze ski jump. Bring your camera along: from the lower walking path, the golden afternoon sunlight offers the most beautiful perspective of the castle turrets framed against the dark mountain forests of the Martinswand.
